interest: Narcotics diplomacy, Anslinger's agents in Japan and Japanese drug monopolies in China.
keywords: League of Nations Opium Advisory Committee
overview: This file consists of twenty-one docket binder sheets (Jacket Case Sheets 16 through 36) from the U.S. State Department's central decimal file 894.114 (Traffic in Liquors and Habit-Forming Drugs: Japan), recording document sub-numbers 152 through 371 dated from December 1934 to December 1939. It provides an extensive chronological register of diplomatic correspondence, consular despatches, Treasury reports, intelligence memoranda, and League of Nations documents concerning illicit narcotics manufacture and trafficking involving Japan. Major subjects documented include illicit maritime smuggling networks operating trans-Pacific routes (notably aboard NYK liners such as the Heian Maru, Taiyo Maru, and Chichibu Maru) between Japanese ports (Kobe, Yokohama) and the United States (Seattle, San Francisco, Honolulu); Japanese complicity in large-scale opium and heroin distribution in occupied China, Manchuria, and Jehol; domestic Japanese drug enforcement, legislation, addiction clinics, and legal scandals (such as the Tsunemitsu and Mitani bribery cases); and bilateral coordination and friction between U.S. Treasury and State Department officials and the Japanese Metropolitan Police and Foreign Office, highlighted by the official U.S. visit of police officer Shinji Taniguchi.

subfiles.about: A continuous 21-sheet docket register (Jacket Case Sheets 16–36) listing and summarizing State Department correspondence, despatches, telegrams, and cross-reference entries on narcotics traffic in Japan from December 1934 to December 1939.
subfiles.summary: This document comprises the complete twenty-one sheets of the State Department's Jacket Case / List of Papers for central decimal file 894.114 (Traffic in Narcotics: Japan), recording document entries sub-numbered 152 through 371 between December 1934 and December 1939. The docket indexes diplomatic despatches, consular reports, and inter-departmental communications with the Treasury and Labor Departments concerning illicit trans-Pacific smuggling operations, League of Nations proceedings, and narcotics distribution in Japanese-controlled China. It also records bilateral administrative arrangements, including investigations of maritime smuggling aboard Japanese liners, Japanese domestic legislation and addiction treatment, and official liaison between U.S. and Japanese police authorities.
